surprises.head: Jesper Wallstedt stole one
surprises.body: Wallstedt allowed 1 goal on 28 shots, worth 3.5 expected goals: 2.5 fewer than expected. That is more than Minnesota’s winning margin. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 30 starts.

story.head: Wallstedt stands on his head against the Canadiens
paras: Montréal had a goal taken off after a video review midway through the first. The league looked at a Canadiens chance later in the period on video and ruled no goal. Bobby Brink got the scoring started for the Wild early in the third. With the goalie pulled and less than two minutes left, Nick Suzuki tied it 1-1 for Montréal. Kirill Kaprizov won it on the power play 21 seconds into overtime.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. The Canadiens hit two posts and the crossbar and still lost. Jesper Wallstedt made 27 saves for the Wild, and Jacob Fowler kept the Habs in it, stopping 22 of 24. The Wild improved to 13-3-4, tied for first in the NHL in points, while the Canadiens fell to 11-3-4, second in the Atlantic.

items.text: Kirill Kaprizov moved into a tie for ninth in overtime goals since the NHL went to 3-on-3 overtime in 2015-16, with 15.
The Canadiens have points in eleven straight games (8-0-3), the longest run in the league right now.
The Wild have points in nine straight games (7-0-2).
The Wild’s Jared Spurgeon was back in the lineup after missing five games.
